_説明: Explanations shown when you click a word in the code (English). tools/make_glossaries.py makes this file from the dictionaries in tools/glossary/en/ (fix the dictionaries, not this file).
numpy: A library for fast calculations on arrays of numbers (vectors and matrices)
np: Uses NumPy under the short name np (import numpy as np)
np.array: Makes a NumPy array (a vector or matrix)
array: Makes a NumPy array (a vector or matrix)
arange: Makes an array of evenly spaced numbers. np.arange(0, 10, 2) is 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
reshape: Changes an array's shape (numbers of rows and columns). -1 means "decide automatically"
shape: An array's shape (the number of elements in each direction). (rows, columns)
ndim: The number of an array's dimensions (1 for a vector, 2 for a matrix)
size: The total number of an array's elements
dtype: The type of an array's elements (int64, float64 and so on). dtype=float makes them decimals
std: The standard deviation. ddof=1 divides by n−1 (unbiased)
axis: The direction to calculate in. axis=0 is down (per column), axis=1 is across (per row)
argmax: The position (index) of the largest value
where: Uses the first value where the condition holds and the second where it does not
default_rng: Makes a random number generator. With a seed, you get the same random numbers every time
normal: Random numbers from a normal distribution. normal(mean, standard deviation, count)
integers: Random integers. integers(low, high, count) (high is not included)
choice: Picks at random from an array
sqrt: Square root (element by element for arrays)
sin: Sine. Element by element for arrays
pandas: A library for handling table data (like Excel)
pd: Uses pandas under the short name pd (import pandas as pd)
Series: One column of pandas data (a named 1-D array)
read_csv: Reads a CSV file into a DataFrame
to_csv: Writes a DataFrame to a CSV file. index=False leaves out the row numbers
to_csv.index: False leaves out the row numbers
loc: Selects rows and columns by name (label). df.loc[row, column]
iloc: Selects rows and columns by number. df.iloc[0, 1]
values: The list of a dictionary's values. In pandas, takes out the contents as a NumPy array
head: The first few rows
sort_values: Sorts by value. ascending=False sorts largest first
sort_values.ascending: True sorts smallest first, False largest first
groupby: Splits into groups by a column's values. Then summarize with mean() and so on
agg: Does several summaries (mean, total and so on) per group at once
query: Selects rows with a condition string. df.query("milk > 30")
isin: Whether a value equals any item in a list
apply: Applies a function to each row or column
rename: Changes column or row names. rename(columns={"old": "new"})
dropna: Removes rows with missing values. subset= chooses the columns to check
dropna.subset: Limits the columns checked for missing values
fillna: Fills missing values with a chosen value
merge: Joins two tables side by side on a shared column (SQL JOIN). on=, how=
merge.how: How to join. "inner" (in both), "left" (keep all of the left) and so on
concat: Joins tables by stacking them (or side by side)
crosstab: A table counting each combination of two columns (a cross-tabulation)
to_datetime: Turns strings into dates and times
dt: The way into the year, month, day and so on of a date column (df["date"].dt.month)
days: The number of days in a length of time
pyplot: The collection of matplotlib's graph-drawing functions
plt: Uses matplotlib.pyplot under the short name plt
subplots: Makes the graph's sheet (fig) and the place to draw the graph (ax)
subplots.figsize: The sheet's size (width, height), in inches
figsize: The sheet's size (width, height), in inches
fig: The sheet for the whole graph (Figure)
ax: The place to draw one graph (Axes)
axes: Several places to draw graphs (Axes) side by side
plot.marker: The shape of the point marks ("o" is a circle)
plot.label: The name shown in the legend
marker: The shape of the point marks ("o" is a circle)
bins: The number of a histogram's bins
legend: Shows the legend (the list of line names)
tight_layout: Arranges things so the text does not overlap
show: Shows the graph on the screen
savefig: Saves the graph to an image file
rcParams: The dictionary of matplotlib settings (such as Japanese fonts)
edgecolor: The color of the edges of bars and points
import: Loads a module (another file or library). You can give it a short name with as, as in import numpy as np
from: Loads only part of a module. from datetime import date
as: Gives another name to something imported, or something opened with with
def: Makes a function. After def name(arguments):, write the body indented
return: Returns the function's answer and ends the function
class: Makes a class (a blueprint bundling data and functions)
self: Inside a method, refers to "this object itself". Written as the method's first argument
__init__: The method called first when an object is made (the constructor). Sets the initial values
__name__: The current file's name. It is '__main__' only when the file is run directly
__str__: A special method that decides how the object looks when turned into text with print() or str()
__lt__: A special method that defines comparison with < (used when sorting)
super: Calls the parent class. super().__init__() runs the parent's initialization
if: Runs only when the condition is true
elif: When the previous if was not true, checks another condition (else if)
else: Runs when none of the conditions matched
for: Takes the contents of a container one at a time and repeats
while: Repeats while the condition is true
in: In for, "one at a time from..."; in a condition, "whether it is in..."
or: True when at least one is true
is: Whether two things are the same object. Used to check for None, as in x is None
continue: Skips the rest of this round of the loop and goes to the next
match: Branches by the shape of a value (from Python 3.10). Combined with case
case: Inside match, one shape to match. case _: means "everything else"
try: Wraps code where an error may occur
except: What to do when an error occurs inside try. You can specify the kind, as in except ValueError:
finally: Always runs at the end, whether or not an error occurred
with: Opens a file or the like and closes it automatically when done
lambda: Makes a small unnamed function on the spot. lambda x: x * 2
del: Deletes a variable or an element of a list
print.sep: The text put between several values (default: one space)
print.end: The text added at the end (default: a newline)
input: Reads one line from the keyboard (returned as a string)
len: The length (number of elements or characters)
range: Makes a run of integers. range(5) is 0–4, range(1, 6) is 1–5
list: Makes a list (an ordered, changeable container)
set: Makes a set (a container with no duplicates)
int: An integer. int("3") turns a string into an integer
float: A decimal (floating-point number). float("2.5") turns a string into a decimal
str: A string. str(3) turns a number into a string
type: Checks the type of a value
round: Rounds (to the nearest even number at .5). round(x, 1) gives 1 decimal place
sorted: Returns a new sorted list. key= sets what to sort by, reverse=True sorts largest first
sorted.key: A function that decides what to sort by. key=lambda c: c["milk"]
enumerate: Takes out a number and an item as a pair, one at a time
enumerate.start: The number to start counting from (default: 0)
zip: Takes items at the same position from several containers as pairs
open: Opens a file. "r" reads, "w" writes (overwrites), "a" appends
open.encoding: The character encoding. For Japanese, use encoding="utf-8"
open.newline: How newlines are handled. Use newline="" when writing csv
append: Adds to the end of a list
insert: Adds at a given position in a list. insert(0, x) adds at the front
pop: Takes an item out of a list and removes it (the last one if no position is given)
remove: Finds that value in a list and removes it
items: Takes out a dictionary's key–value pairs one at a time
keys: The list of a dictionary's keys
get: Gets a value from a dictionary. If the key is missing, returns None (or the second argument)
strip: Removes spaces and newlines at both ends
split: Splits a string at a separator into a list
join: Joins the strings in a list with text in between. ", ".join(names)
math: A module of math functions (sqrt, pi, sin and so on)
pi: π, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
json: A module for reading and writing JSON files
dump: Writes to a file as JSON
load: Reads a JSON file into dictionaries and lists
dump.ensure_ascii: False writes Japanese and other non-ASCII text as it is
dump.indent: The indent width. Makes the JSON easy to read
csv: A module for reading and writing CSV (comma-separated) files
writer: Makes a tool for writing CSV
DictReader: Reads CSV one row at a time as a dictionary (header → value)
timedelta: A length of time (days, hours). Can be added to or subtracted from dates
dataclass: A marker (@dataclass) that lets you write data-holding classes briefly
field: Settings for a data class field. field(default_factory=list) makes an empty list the default
default_factory: A function that makes the default value. Used when the default is changeable, such as a list
Traceback: The display of the chain of calls when an error occurs. The last line is the error itself
ZeroDivisionError: The error when you divide by 0
ValueError: The error when a value is wrong (int("abc") and so on)
KeyError: The error when you use a key that is not in the dictionary
IndexError: The error when you use a position outside the list
TypeError: The error when types do not match (adding a string and a number and so on)
FileNotFoundError: The error when a file cannot be found
venv: A Python virtual environment (a per-project place for libraries)
pip: The tool for installing Python libraries
$ sudo:
Origin: short for superuser do (run as the administrator).
Runs the following command with administrator rights. Needed to change system settings or install software.
It asks for your password the first time (nothing appears on screen as you type).
$ apt:
Origin: short for Advanced Package Tool.
The command that manages software on Ubuntu. It installs and removes software.
$ apt install:
Installs software from the internet.
Example: sudo apt install pipx installs pipx.
$ cd:
Origin: short for change directory.
Moves to another folder in the terminal.
$ code:
The command that starts VS Code from the terminal.
code collar opens the collar folder in VS Code. code . opens the current folder.
Opens the current folder in VS Code.
Loads a settings file into the current terminal (the same as source)
$ :: A leading : means "a file on the Pico". Without :, it is a file on the PC.
$ |:
Origin: a pipe, like data flowing through a pipe.
Passes the result of the command on the left to the command on the right.
$ python3:
Origin: version 3 of Python.
Runs a Python program on the PC.
$ hello.py: A file on the PC with the code you want to run. You choose the name.
$ mkdir:
Origin: short for make directory.
Makes a folder.
$ mkdir -p:
Origin: -p is short for parents.
Also makes the folders along the way. No error if it already exists.
$ main.py: main.py on the PC. Saved on the Pico under the same name, it runs automatically at power-on.
$ pip:
Origin: said to be short for pip installs packages.
Installs Python libraries. It cannot be used on the Pico.
$ source: Loads settings written in a file into the current terminal. source ~/.bashrc makes settings you just added usable right away.
$ python3 -m: Runs a Python module as a command. python3 -m serial.tools.miniterm runs pyserial's serial monitor.
$ python: Runs Python (the same as python3 inside a virtual environment)
$ venv: The module that makes Python virtual environments
$ .venv/bin/activate: The file that turns on the virtual environment. Load it with source
